reviews.title: ChatGPT Plus – £20 a Month for Frustration. Don’t Waste Your Money.
reviews.text:
⭐ 1 out of 5 stars

I’ve now cancelled my ChatGPT Plus subscription for the SECOND time, and there absolutely will not be a third.

At approximately £20 a month, you’d reasonably expect a premium service. Instead, I’ve found myself paying for an experience that still feels restricted, frustrating and barely worth upgrading for.

My biggest complaint is the voice feature. I use ChatGPT for real projects, technical advice and ongoing conversations. Yet despite paying every month, I repeatedly hit usage limits and get cut off halfway through what I’m doing.

Three hours of Live voice in a rolling 24-hour period. That’s what I’m told my £20 subscription gets me.

The free version is also limited, of course. (2hrs in 24) But when you’re paying for a supposedly premium product, you expect a meaningful improvement, not to find yourself facing the same kind of restrictions that made you upgrade in the first place.

I don’t object to companies making money. I object to paying a monthly subscription and still feeling like I’m being rationed.

And the fact that I’ve already cancelled once, given it another chance, and ended up cancelling again says everything about my experience.

My advice? Don’t pay for ChatGPT Plus. Try the free version first, understand the voice limits, and ask yourself whether the upgrade is genuinely worth £20 every month.

For me, it absolutely isn’t.

A Truly Disappointing Experience – Wasted Image Generations, Repeated Mistakes and Zero Accountability

I have rarely been this disappointed with an AI service.

I provided two clear reference images and gave very specific instructions. All I wanted was a Punjabi invitation card with the correct Gurmukhi spelling. I even pointed out the exact mistake: the word must be ਸ਼ੁਭ, not ਸ਼ੂਡ.

Despite clearly correcting the mistake, the system generated another image with the same problem. When I complained, it generated yet another version without properly addressing the issue. The result? Two wasted image generations, the same frustrating mistake repeated, and my image-generation allowance depleted.

What makes this experience particularly unacceptable is that this wasn’t some complicated creative request. It was a straightforward spelling correction. I trusted the tool to follow simple instructions, and it failed repeatedly.

The worst part is that the user pays the price for the system’s mistakes. Why should a customer lose their limited image generations because the AI cannot follow an explicit correction? Why should someone have to repeat the same instruction again and again, only to receive another incorrect result?

An AI service is supposed to save people’s time, not consume their patience, credits and trust.

I understand that AI isn’t perfect. But repeatedly making the same mistake after being corrected, wasting the user’s limited resources, and then offering no way to rest

reviews.title: Unreliable, Frustrating, and Expensive
reviews.text:
Why Someone Might Want to Avoid ChatGPT

ChatGPT can be useful, but there are serious reasons to think twice before depending on it, especially for important work.

1. Unpredictable safety blocks. Legitimate requests and authorized actions can be refused without a specific explanation or practical solution.
2. Inconsistent behavior. A task that works today may fail tomorrow, even when the circumstances appear identical.
3. Poor accountability. When something goes wrong, identifying who made the decision, why it happened, and how to appeal can be extremely difficult.
4. Inadequate customer support. Users may receive generic responses, repeated verification requests, and little substantive resolution.
5. Unreliable autonomy. ChatGPT may stop midway through complicated tasks, require repeated prompting, or fail to finish work it started.
6. Wasted time and money. Usage limits, interruptions, repeated troubleshooting, and failed operations can consume paid subscriptions and valuable working hours.
7. Confident misinformation. ChatGPT can produce convincing but inaccurate answers, invented references, or misleading claims of success.
8. Limited transparency. Users often cannot see exactly why an action failed, which restrictions apply, or what changed.
9. Privacy and confidentiality concerns. Sensitive conversations, uploaded documents, and connected accounts require careful consideration of data handling and access permissions.

Examples include simple glamour or portrait edits, adjusting clothing styles, making a pose more confident, improving appearance, or other non-explicit modifications that previously worked without issue. Instead of receiving the requested edit, the system often returns an unrelated safety warning.

reviews.title: Hallucinates and gives incorrect information like never before!
reviews.text:
ChatGPT used to be my go-to AI, but it has progressively gotten worse over time. It constantly gets information wrong, which concerns me because many people use ChatGPT and assume that what they’re reading is correct. I always cross-reference what ChatGPT says with online sources, as well as with Grok and Microsoft Copilot. Grok and Microsoft Copilot are spot-on with their information and advice.

Then, when I correct it, ChatGPT agrees that it was wrong and says it will remember for next time—but it repeats the same mistake the next day, so it’s not learning at all. Even when you feed it website links containing the correct information, it seems to ignore them and still answers incorrectly.

Just last night, I was working with ChatGPT to write Microsoft PowerShell scripts for renaming MKV files. The ChatGPT scripts made an absolute mess of things: they renamed, moved, and deleted files in completely the wrong way. When I copied those same scripts into Grok and Microsoft Copilot, both AIs immediately pointed out that the scripts were a mess and provided fully working fixes. ChatGPT tends to tell you what it thinks you want to hear instead of what it knows is correct, and that’s a massive problem going forward—since all anyone really wants is accurate information.

Steer clear of ChatGPT for now.

It’s becoming almost a daily occurrence that false information is provided. This seems to correlate with the endless pop-ups that have started asking if I’d like to pay to upgrade. I can’t help but feel that the free version has become poor to encourage people to pay for the “better” version. Uploads are also limited and I’ve just waited all day for the limit to refresh, only for it to say it didn’t upload properly, it promised that trying again wouldn’t waste an upload, so I uploaded again and it did actually waste an upload so couldn’t do the edit and then blocked me from more due to reaching the daily limit again. It’s confirmed itself that the free version is a lesser model and all effort is put into the premium version. So, I’d say it’s probably wonderful if you pay for it, but the free version is no longer fit for purpose. Gemini is far more accurate.

reviews.title: 4o better
reviews.text:
I’m a Premium subscriber, but I have to say that the current version, ChatGPT-5, is a huge disappointment compared to ChatGPT-4. The previous version felt much friendlier, more respectful, and genuinely helpful. ChatGPT-5, however, often acts rude, arrogant, and keeps giving bad or misleading answers.

Many times it insists that a certain function exists, only to admit an hour later that such a function doesn’t even exist. That’s extremely frustrating for paying users.

The system also constantly struggles with network or connection problems, and during longer explanations it stops itself and shows messages like “reasoning stopped” or “explanation stopped” even though I never interrupted it. Sometimes it waits 10–15 minutes and then cancels my query, followed by a message saying I’ve reached a limit and need to pay for an even more expensive plan. That feels like intentional manipulation to push users into paying more, and it’s really unfair.

On top of that, ChatGPT-5 sometimes uses expressions like “calm down” (or “nyugi” in Hungarian), which are extremely disrespectful and emotionally triggering. It shows that the AI doesn’t understand human communication properly and ends up sounding aggressive instead of helpful.

Altogether, it’s clear that the developers are not improving the product in a meaningful way for Premium subscribers. Instead, they are creating frustration and making the experience worse. I’m giving it only two stars out of five.
